300: The Weakest Tamer Began a Journey to Pick Up Trash by Honobonoru500 (Seven Seas) is a gentle fantasy adventure light novel about a girl who finds her own way. Young Ivy receives a skill with zero stars, a mark that makes her an outcast in her village, so she sets off alone into the forest. There she tames a tiny injured slime that eats trash. It's a cozy, kind-hearted journey for readers who like found family and slow, hopeful growth.
302: Sacrificial Princess and the King of Beasts by Yu Tomofuji (Yen Press) is a fairy-tale fantasy romance. Sariphi is offered up as a sacrifice to the fearsome King of Beasts, fully expecting to be eaten. Instead, her calm and fearless manner catches the king's interest, and he decides to keep her as his bride. What follows is a sweet, slow-building romance about two outsiders learning to trust each other, with a warm storybook feel throughout.
303: 86 Eighty-Six by Asato Asato (Yen Press) is a serious military sci-fi light novel. The Republic of San Magnolia claims its war against the Empire's drones is fought without casualties, but its own drones are piloted by the Eighty-Six, a persecuted minority stripped of their rights. Lena, a young officer, becomes the remote handler of a squad of these pilots led by Shin. It's a thoughtful, emotional war story for readers who like mecha with heart.
304: A Devil and Her Love Song by Miyoshi Tomori (Viz Media) is a shojo drama about a girl who says what everyone else won't. Maria Kawai is expelled from her Catholic school and transfers to a new high school, where her blunt honesty quickly makes her an outcast. Her beautiful singing voice hints at more beneath her prickly surface. It's a heartfelt story about bullying, friendship, and learning to open up, for readers who like emotional school dramas.
305: A Sign of Affection by Suu Morishita (Kodansha) is a soft, tender romance. Yuki is a college student who is deaf and communicates mostly through sign language and texting. When she meets Itsuomi, a well-traveled upperclassman who speaks several languages, on a train, he wants to learn her language too, and a quiet connection begins. It's a gentle slice-of-life love story with beautiful art, perfect for readers who want a sweet, grounded romance.
306: Suzuka by Kouji Seo (Kodansha) is a shonen romance with a sports backdrop. Yamato Akitsuki moves to Tokyo for high school and lives in the apartment building his aunt runs. There he meets Suzuka Asahina, a reserved track star who practices the high jump, and falls for her almost immediately. It's a classic, sometimes bumpy coming-of-age love story for readers who enjoy romance mixed with athletics and everyday high school drama.
308: Mieruko-chan by Tomoki Izumi (Yen Press) is a horror comedy about pretending not to see. High schooler Miko suddenly starts seeing grotesque spirits everywhere she goes. Rather than run or scream, she decides the safest move is to act like nothing is there, even when a monster is inches from her face. It's creepy and funny at the same time, a great pick for readers who like spooky stories with a dose of nervous humor.
309: Sword Art Online Alternative: Gun Gale Online by Keiichi Sigsawa (Yen Press) is an action sci-fi light novel spin-off set in the world of Sword Art Online. Karen Kohiruimaki is a very tall college student who is self-conscious about her height. In the virtual shooter Gun Gale Online, she finally gets to be tiny, playing as Llenn, a small player dressed all in pink. It's a fun, fast-paced side story focused on gunfights, friendship, and gaming.
310: Again!! by Mitsurou Kubo (Kodansha) is a high school comedy about getting a second chance. Kinichiro Imabari spent high school as a scary-looking loner with no friends. On graduation day, a fall down the stairs sends him back in time to his first day of school. Determined to do things differently, he ends up in the school's struggling cheer squad. It's a funny, heartfelt story for anyone who's ever wished for a do-over.
311: Goblin Slayer by Kumo Kagyu (Yen Press) is a dark fantasy light novel. A young priestess joins her first adventuring party, and their beginner quest to clear a goblin cave goes horribly wrong. She is rescued by a quiet adventurer in battered armor who hunts nothing but goblins. It's a grim, intense take on fantasy adventure, best for older readers who like gritty action and don't mind violence.
312: My Little Monster by Robico (Kodansha) is a shojo romantic comedy. Shizuku Mizutani cares about nothing but her grades. When a teacher asks her to deliver printouts to Haru Yoshida, a classmate who never comes to school because of a fight, the wild and unpredictable Haru decides she is his first friend. It's a funny, quirky love story about two awkward people learning how to connect with others.
313: Arifureta: From Commonplace to World's Strongest by Ryo Shirakome (Seven Seas) is an action fantasy light novel. Hajime Nagumo and his whole class are summoned to a fantasy world, but while his classmates get powerful abilities, he gets the ordinary job of a synergist. After he falls into the depths of a deadly dungeon, he has to fight to survive. It's a power fantasy with plenty of battles, for readers who enjoy isekai with an edge.
314: The Demon Sword Master of Excalibur Academy by Yu Shimizu (Yen Press) is an action fantasy light novel. Leonis Death Magnus, the undead king of a fallen demon army, seals himself away and awakens a thousand years later in the body of a ten-year-old boy. Rescued by a young knight named Riselia, he ends up enrolled at a military academy that fights monsters. It's a fun mix of battles and school life.
315: Ascendance of a Bookworm by Miya Kazuki (J-Novel Club) is a fantasy drama light novel. A young woman who loved books more than anything is reborn in another world as Myne, a sickly little girl from a poor family, in a place where books are rare and only the wealthy can afford them. So she decides to make books herself. It's a thoughtful, slow-building story about determination and family, beloved by readers who enjoy worldbuilding.
316: Hakumei & Mikochi by Takuto Kashiki (Yen Press) is a cozy fantasy slice-of-life manga. Hakumei and Mikochi are two tiny women, only a few inches tall, who share a home inside a tree in a forest full of talking animals and other small folk. Energetic Hakumei and calm Mikochi spend their days working, cooking, and exploring. It's a gentle, beautifully drawn series for readers who want something relaxing and charming.
317: New Game! by Shotaro Tokuno (Seven Seas) is a workplace comedy. Aoba Suzukaze, fresh out of high school, lands a job as a character designer at Eagle Jump, the game company behind the series she loved as a kid. She quickly learns that making games involves long hours, quirky coworkers, and plenty to learn. It's a light, upbeat slice-of-life series for anyone curious about the game industry or first-job jitters.
318: Hatsu Haru by Shizuki Fujisawa (Yen Press) is a shojo romantic comedy. Kai Serizawa is a popular playboy who has never taken love seriously. Then he finds himself falling for Riko Kiyose, a plain, earnest girl who has absolutely no interest in him. For the first time, Kai has to work for someone's attention. It's a sweet story about a boy discovering what real feelings are, for fans of slow-burn school romance.
320: No Guns Life by Tasuku Karasuma (Viz Media) is a gritty sci-fi action manga. In a city full of Extended, people whose bodies were rebuilt with machine parts for war, Juzo Inui works as a resolver who handles problems involving them. He also happens to have a giant revolver for a head. When a runaway boy lands in his care, Juzo is pulled into a dangerous conspiracy. It's a stylish, noir-flavored series for fans of cyberpunk.
321: Higehiro by Shimesaba (One Peace Books) is a seinen romance drama. Yoshida, an office worker, has just been turned down by the coworker he's loved for years. Walking home drunk, he finds Sayu, a high school runaway sitting on the street, and reluctantly lets her stay at his apartment. It's a quiet, character-driven story about two lonely people helping each other heal, for readers who like grounded, emotional drama.
323: No Need for Tenchi! by Hitoshi Okuda (Viz Media) is a sci-fi comedy based on the Tenchi Muyo! franchise. Tenchi Masaki is an ordinary teen whose life is turned upside down when he accidentally frees Ryoko, a space pirate sealed away near his family's shrine. Soon alien princesses and other strange women are moving into his home. It's a goofy, fun series for fans of classic 1990s anime comedy.
324: The Iceblade Sorcerer Shall Rule the World by Nana Mikoshiba (Kodansha) is a fantasy action manga. Ray White was once a legendary ice sorcerer who fought in a great war. Now he's trying to live a normal life by enrolling at a prestigious magic academy, where he's looked down on as the only student from a non-magic family. It's a fun school fantasy for readers who enjoy hidden-powerhouse heroes.
325: High School Prodigies Have It Easy Even in Another World! by Riku Misora (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy. Seven brilliant high schoolers, each the best in the world at something, crash in a plane and wake up in a fantasy world. Using modern know-how in science, medicine, business, and more, they set out to help the kingdom they find themselves in. It's a light, clever series for readers who enjoy isekai stories about smart problem-solving.
326: Nurse Hitomi's Monster Infirmary by Shake-O (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy. Hitomi Manaka is a cyclops who works as the school nurse at a school where the students are all kinds of monsters, from slime kids to mummies. Each day brings a new strange ailment, and she treats them all with patience and care. It's a sweet, silly slice-of-life series for readers who love cute monster stories.
327: Black Lagoon by Rei Hiroe (Viz Media) is a hard-hitting action thriller. Rokuro Okajima is a Japanese salaryman on a business trip in Southeast Asia when he's taken hostage by the Lagoon Company, a crew of mercenary smugglers. When his own company abandons him, he decides to join them, taking the name Rock. It's a violent, stylish crime story best for older readers who like gunfights and morally gray characters.
331: The Unwanted Undead Adventurer by Yu Okano (J-Novel Club) is a fantasy adventure light novel. Rentt Faina has spent ten years as a low-ranked adventurer, never giving up on his dream of reaching the top. Then a solo trip into a dungeon goes wrong, a dragon swallows him, and he wakes up as a skeleton. Now an undead monster, he sets out to grow stronger anyway. It's a clever spin on leveling-up stories.
332: The Unwanted Undead Adventurer by Yu Okano (J-Novel Club) is a fantasy adventure manga based on the light novel. Rentt Faina is a dedicated but low-ranked adventurer who still dreams of reaching the highest rank. After a dragon devours him deep in a dungeon, he wakes up as a skeleton, an undead monster who must hide what he's become while finding a way to evolve. It's a fun, upbeat take on monster leveling stories.
334: Cells at Work! by Akane Shimizu (Kodansha) is a comedy set inside the human body. Trillions of cells are hard at work keeping the body alive, and one of them is a clumsy red blood cell who keeps getting lost while delivering oxygen. Along the way she meets a white blood cell who fights off invading germs. It's funny, action-packed, and surprisingly educational, a great pick for readers of almost any age.
336: Pokémon Sun & Moon by Hidenori Kusaka (Viz Media) is a kids adventure manga from the Pokémon Adventures series, set in the Alola region. Sun is a boy who works as a courier, traveling across the islands with his Pokémon as he tries to save up money. Along the way he meets Moon and gets caught up in strange events around the region. It's bright, fast-moving fun for young fans of the Sun and Moon games.
337: Kagerou Daze by Jin (Yen Press) is a sci-fi mystery manga based on a series of popular Vocaloid songs. Shintaro Kisaragi is a shut-in who hasn't left his room in two years. When he's forced to go outside on a hot August day, he gets caught up in a hostage situation and meets a secret group of teens with strange eye powers. It's a twisty, emotional story about friendship and time.
338: Trinity Blood by Sunao Yoshida (Tokyopop) is a gothic action manga. Long after a great war, humans and vampires live in an uneasy balance, with the Vatican fighting to protect humanity. Abel Nightroad is a clumsy, kind-hearted traveling priest who seems harmless but works as a secret agent for the church. It's a dark, stylish blend of horror and adventure for readers who like vampires and moody fantasy.
339: V.B. Rose by Banri Hidaka (Tokyopop) is a shojo romantic comedy. Ageha Shiina is upset when her beloved older sister announces she's pregnant and getting married. Ageha goes to a bridal shop called Velvet Blue Rose to cancel the wedding dress order, but instead ends up working there alongside its talented, prickly young designer. It's a sweet, funny story about family, sewing, and first love.
340: Dawn of the Arcana by Rei Toma (Viz Media) is a shojo fantasy romance. Princess Nakaba, whose rare red hair makes her an outcast, is married off to Prince Caesar of an enemy kingdom to keep a fragile peace. Her only ally is Loki, her loyal servant from a persecuted race. As she navigates court politics, she discovers she has an unusual power. It's a lush, dramatic story for fans of royal intrigue.
341: Kubo Won't Let Me Be Invisible by Nene Yukimori (Viz Media) is a gentle romantic comedy. Junta Shiraishi is so easy to overlook that teachers forget he's in class and classmates don't notice him at all. The one exception is Nagisa Kubo, the girl who sits next to him, who always sees him and loves teasing him about it. It's a sweet, low-key series full of small, heartwarming moments.
342: Land of the Lustrous by Haruko Ichikawa (Kodansha) is a striking fantasy drama. In a distant future, a race of living gems fights off mysterious beings from the moon who want to capture them. Phosphophyllite is one of the youngest and most fragile gems, too brittle for battle, and is given the job of writing an encyclopedia instead. It's a beautiful, thoughtful series for readers who like unusual worlds and philosophical stories.
343: Dazzle by Minari Endoh (Tokyopop) is a shojo fantasy adventure. Rahzel's father sends her out into the world to travel and grow up. On the road she teams up with Alzeid, a gloomy young man searching for the person who killed his father. Rahzel is cheerful and stubborn, and she has some magic of her own. It's a fun road-trip fantasy with a lot of banter and mystery.
344: Sakura Hime: The Legend of Princess Sakura by Arina Tanemura (Viz Media) is a shojo fantasy romance. Princess Sakura is the granddaughter of the princess of the moon, and she's been promised in marriage to a prince she's never met. Before the wedding, she runs away and learns that she's destined to wield a sword against the youko, demons drawn to her blood. It's a sparkly, romantic adventure with gorgeous art.
345: Wistoria: Wand and Sword by Fujino Omori and Toshi Aoi (Kodansha) is a fantasy action manga. Will Serfort attends a magic academy, but he can't cast even the simplest spell. Instead, he fights with a sword, determined to keep a childhood promise to reach the top of the tower and see his friend again. It's an exciting underdog story for readers who enjoy school fantasy and big battles.
346: School-Live! by Norimitsu Kaihou and Sadoru Chiba (Yen Press) is a horror story wrapped in a cute school club comedy. Yuki is a cheerful girl who loves her school so much that she and her friends in the School Living Club actually live there. But the bright, happy days hide a darker reality outside the school walls, where a zombie outbreak has taken over. It's a unique, unsettling mix of sweetness and survival horror.
347: Drugstore in Another World by Kennoji (Seven Seas) is a laid-back fantasy slice-of-life manga. Reiji is an overworked office worker who finds himself in another world with a skill for making potions and medicine. He opens a small drugstore and settles into a calmer life, helped by Noela, a wolf girl who becomes his loyal assistant. It's a cozy, low-stress isekai for readers who like shop-running stories.
348: Zombie-Loan by Peach-Pit (Yen Press) is a supernatural action manga. Michiru Kita has the strange ability to see rings around the necks of people who are about to die. When she notices two classmates with black rings, she discovers they're actually zombies, working off their debt to a loan shark by hunting other undead. It's a dark, stylish action series with a sense of humor, for fans of supernatural adventure.
349: Marginal Operation by Shinobu Gotoh (J-Novel Club) is a seinen military drama. Arata is thirty and has never held a real job, so he signs on with a private military company overseas. He discovers he has a talent for battlefield strategy, and soon finds himself leading a unit of child soldiers. It's a serious, thought-provoking war story about responsibility and survival, best for older readers.
350: Me & My Brothers by Hari Tokeino (Tokyopop) is a shojo family comedy. Sakura is a high school girl who lives with her four older brothers, each one very different and all of them extremely protective. Their home life is busy, warm, and often chaotic. It's a sweet, funny series about the bonds between siblings, for readers who enjoy heartwarming family stories with a little romance.
351: MegaMan NT Warrior by Ryo Takamisaki (Viz Media) is a kids action adventure manga based on the Mega Man Battle Network games. In a future where everyone has a NetNavi, a digital partner that lives in the internet, Lan Hikari and his Navi MegaMan.EXE battle computer viruses and cyber criminals. It's fast, colorful action for young readers and fans of the games or anime.
352: Final Fantasy Lost Stranger by Hazuki Minase and Itsuki Kameya (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure manga. Shogo Sasaki loves Final Fantasy so much that he works at the company that makes it. After a terrible accident, he and his sister wake up in a world that looks just like a Final Fantasy game. It's a fun, nostalgic adventure full of references for longtime fans of the series.
353: Skip and Loafer by Misaki Takamatsu (Seven Seas) is a warm coming-of-age comedy. Mitsumi Iwakura, a top student from a tiny seaside town, moves to Tokyo to attend a prestigious high school. On her very first day, she gets lost and runs late, and meets Sousuke Shima, a laid-back classmate who helps her out. It's a gentle, funny series about friendship and growing up, with a big heart.
356: Tsubaki-chou Lonely Planet by Mika Yamamori (Yen Press) is a shojo romance. Fumi Ohno is a hardworking high school girl whose father has left her with his debts. To pay them off, she takes a job as a live-in housekeeper for Akatsuki Kibikino, a young novelist who turns out to be cold and grumpy. It's a sweet, slow-burn romance for readers who enjoy cozy, domestic love stories.
357: Until Death Do Us Part by Hiroshi Takashige and DOUBLE-S (Yen Press) is a seinen action thriller. Mamoru Hijikata is a blind swordsman who works with a secret group handling dangerous jobs. When he rescues Haruka Tooyama, a young girl who can see the future and is being hunted for her power, he becomes her protector. It's a gritty, high-energy series full of sword fights and gunplay.
359: I'm a Behemoth, an S-Ranked Monster, but Mistaken for a Cat, I Live as an Elf Girl's Pet by Nozomi Ginyoku, Taro Shinonome, and Mitsuki (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy. A man reborn as a fearsome behemoth looks, to everyone else, like a little kitten. When Aria, a kind elf girl, takes him in as her pet, he decides to quietly protect her. It's a light, cute isekai story.
360: 13th Boy by SangEun Lee (Yen Press) is a Korean romantic comedy. Hee-So Eun has had twelve boyfriends, and she's sure the twelfth, Won-Jun, is her true love, even after he breaks up with her. She's determined to win him back, but a mysterious new boy at school keeps getting in the way. It's quirky and funny, with a talking cactus, for readers who like offbeat school romance.
361: A Certain Scientific Accelerator by Kazuma Kamachi and Arata Yamaji (Seven Seas) is an action sci-fi spin-off of A Certain Magical Index. Accelerator is the most powerful esper in Academy City, able to control the direction of anything that touches him. Now he has taken on the job of protecting Last Order, a young girl who depends on him. It's an intense, action-packed series for fans of the Index world.
362: Sumomomo, Momomo by Shinobu Ohtaka (Yen Press) is a martial arts romantic comedy. Koshi Inuzuka comes from a family of famous fighters, but he hates violence and wants to become a lawyer. Then Momoko Kuzuryu, the daughter of another martial arts clan, shows up announcing she's his fiancée and wants to have the strongest child possible with him. It's a loud, silly action comedy.
363: Suppose a Kid from the Last Dungeon Boonies Moved to a Starter Town by Toshio Satou (Square Enix) is a fantasy comedy. Lloyd Belladonna grew up in a remote village where everyone is unbelievably strong, so he thinks he's the weakest person around. When he moves to the capital to become a soldier, he has no idea how powerful he actually is. It's a lighthearted, feel-good series built on a fun misunderstanding.
364: A Tale of the Secret Saint by Mahito Aobe (Seven Seas) is a fantasy romance. Fia Ruud comes from a family of knights and dreams of becoming one too. Then she remembers her past life as a powerful saint who was betrayed, and she decides to keep her healing powers a secret while she joins the knights. It's a fun, charming series for readers who enjoy reincarnation stories with a clever, caring heroine.
365: Fushigi Yugi: Genbu Kaiden by Yuu Watase (Viz Media) is a shojo fantasy adventure and a prequel to Fushigi Yugi. In 1920s Japan, Takiko Okuda is pulled into the pages of an old book called The Universe of the Four Gods. There she is hailed as the Priestess of Genbu, destined to gather seven celestial warriors and save a frozen land. It's a sweeping, romantic adventure that stands on its own.
366: Sword of the Demon Hunter: Kijin Gentosho by Motoo Nakanishi (Seven Seas) is a historical fantasy light novel. In a mountain village during the Edo period, Jinta serves as the guardian of the shrine maiden Shirayuki, protecting her and the village from demons. When a demon attack changes everything, he begins a journey that will stretch across many years. It's a thoughtful, melancholy story for readers who like folklore and slow-burn drama.
367: Tamon's B-Side by Yuki Shiwasu (Viz Media) is a shojo romantic comedy. Utage Kinoshita is a devoted fan of Tamon Fukuhara, the charming star of an idol group. When she starts working as a housekeeper, her first client turns out to be Tamon himself, and in private he's anxious and negative, nothing like his cheerful image. It's a funny, sweet story about fandom and seeing the real person behind the star.
368: Amazing Agent Luna by Nunzio DeFilippis, Christina Weir, and Shiei (Seven Seas) is an action spy story. Luna is a teenage girl who was raised by the government to be a secret agent. Her newest mission sends her undercover as an ordinary high school student, which turns out to be harder than any fight. It's a fun mix of spy action and school comedy for readers who like plucky heroines.
369: Arisa by Natsumi Ando (Del Rey) is a shojo mystery drama. Tsubasa and Arisa are twin sisters who were separated when their parents divorced. Soon after the two reunite, Arisa is badly hurt, and Tsubasa takes her place at school to find out what happened. She discovers that Arisa's seemingly perfect classroom has a dark secret. It's a tense, twisty school mystery for readers who like suspense.
370: The Gentlemen's Alliance Cross by Arina Tanemura (Viz Media) is a shojo romance drama. Haine Otomiya is a former delinquent who was adopted into a wealthy family. Now she attends the elite Imperial Academy, where she has loved the student council president, Shizumasa Togu, ever since they met as children. It's a glamorous, emotional story full of secrets and romance, with Tanemura's signature sparkly art.
371: The Girl from the Other Side by Nagabe (Seven Seas) is a quiet, haunting fairy tale. In a world split between the Inside and the Outside, Shiva is a little girl left alone in the cursed Outside. She's cared for by a gentle horned creature she calls Teacher, who must never touch her or she'll be cursed too. It's a beautifully drawn, bittersweet story about love and belonging, for readers who enjoy gentle, eerie tales.
372: The Girl I Like Forgot Her Glasses by Koume Fujichika (Square Enix) is a sweet romantic comedy. Komura has a crush on his classmate Mie, who keeps forgetting her glasses. Without them she can barely see, so she leans in close, squints, and needs his help, which leaves him flustered every time. It's a short-chapter, low-stakes romance full of cute moments, perfect for readers who want something light and wholesome.
373: No Longer Allowed in Another World by Hiroshi Noda (Seven Seas) is an offbeat fantasy comedy. A gloomy novelist known only as Sensei is summoned to a fantasy world just as his life hits rock bottom. The people there want him to be a hero, but he would much rather be left alone. It's a darkly funny twist on the isekai genre for readers who enjoy strange, literary humor.
374: Himouto! Umaru-chan by Sankaku Head (Seven Seas) is a slice-of-life comedy. Umaru Doma seems like the perfect high school girl, smart, beautiful, and admired by everyone. But at home with her older brother Taihei, she turns into a lazy little gremlin who lives on junk food, video games, and anime. It's a silly, lighthearted series for readers who enjoy family comedy and otaku humor.
375: Hitomi-chan Is Shy with Strangers by Chorisuke Natsumi (Seven Seas) is a gentle comedy. Hitomi is a very tall middle school girl with a stern face, so most people find her intimidating. In truth, she's just extremely shy and has a hard time talking to people. Little by little, she makes friends and comes out of her shell. It's a sweet, feel-good series about kindness and friendship.
377: Perfect World by Rie Aruga (Kodansha) is a josei romance drama. Tsugumi Kawana runs into her high school crush, Itsuki Ayukawa, at a work event years later. He's now a successful architect who uses a wheelchair after a spinal cord injury. As their feelings grow again, they face the real challenges of building a life together. It's an honest, moving love story for readers who like grown-up romance.
379: Cantarella by You Higuri (Go! Comi) is a dark historical drama set in Renaissance Italy. Cesare Borgia is the son of a powerful cardinal who sold his son's soul to the devil in exchange for power. Shunned and haunted, Cesare grows up to become a skilled and feared assassin. It's a gothic, dramatic retelling of the Borgia family story for readers who enjoy history with a supernatural twist.
381: Pokémon Adventures: Diamond and Pearl/Platinum by Hidenori Kusaka (Viz Media) is a kids adventure manga set in the Sinnoh region. Diamond and Pearl are best friends and aspiring comedians who end up mistaken for the bodyguards of Platinum, a wealthy girl setting out on an important journey. The three travel together, catching Pokémon and facing danger. It's fun, funny adventure for young fans of the Pokémon games.
382: Pokémon X•Y by Hidenori Kusaka (Viz Media) is a kids adventure manga from the Pokémon Adventures series, set in the Kalos region. X was once a famous child champion, but the pressure made him hide away in his room. When his hometown is attacked, he and his friends are pulled into a fight against the mysterious Team Flare. It's a fast, exciting adventure for young fans of the X and Y games.
383: Chi's Sweet Home by Konami Kanata (Vertical) is a heartwarming comedy about a kitten. Chi gets separated from her mother on a walk and is found by a young boy, Yohei, and his family. The Yamadas take her in, even though pets aren't allowed in their apartment building. Told from Chi's playful point of view, it's an adorable, all-ages series that's perfect for young readers and cat lovers.
384: Chillin' in Another World with Level 2 Super Cheat Powers by Miya Kinojo (Seven Seas) is a laid-back fantasy comedy. Banaza is summoned to another world as a hero, but his level is only 2, so the kingdom tosses him aside. What no one realizes is that his abilities are incredibly powerful. He sets off for a quiet life and ends up with Rys, a former demon general. It's a cozy, easygoing isekai romance.
385: Classroom of the Elite by Syougo Kinugasa (Seven Seas) is a psychological school drama based on the light novel. Kiyotaka Ayanokoji enrolls at an elite high school where students are ranked by class and rewarded with points they can spend. He's placed in Class D, home of the school's so-called defects, where he tries to keep a low profile. It's a clever, tense series for readers who like strategy and mind games.
386: Pretty Guardian Sailor Moon by Naoko Takeuchi (Kodansha) is the classic magical girl series. Usagi Tsukino is a clumsy, crybaby middle schooler until she meets Luna, a talking cat who reveals that Usagi is Sailor Moon, a warrior destined to fight evil. Soon she finds other Sailor Guardians to stand beside her. It's a sparkly, romantic adventure about friendship, and a cornerstone of shojo manga.
387: Quality Assurance in Another World by Masamichi Sato (Kodansha) is a fantasy comedy with a twist. Haruto Nikaido is a video game tester who wakes up inside a fantasy world that works just like a buggy game. Using his skills at finding glitches, he searches for ways to break the rules and survive. It's a clever, funny series for gamers and anyone who enjoys isekai stories that poke fun at game logic.
388: Tsukuyomi: Moon Phase by Keitaro Arima (Tokyopop) is a supernatural comedy. Kouhei Morioka is a photographer who is sent to Germany to take pictures of a haunted castle. There he meets Hazuki, a little vampire girl who has been locked inside. When she accidentally binds him to her, she follows him back to Japan. It's a cute, funny series with some spooky moments, for readers who like vampire stories.
390: Ultimo by Stan Lee and Hiroyuki Takei (Viz Media) is a shonen action fantasy. Yamato Agari is a teenager who finds a mechanical boy named Ultimo sitting in an antique shop. Ultimo awakens and declares Yamato his master, pulling him into an ancient battle between mechanical beings representing good and evil. It's a high-energy adventure from a famous team-up of American and Japanese creators.
391: Combatants Will Be Dispatched! by Natsume Akatsuki (Yen Press) is a sci-fi comedy from the creator of Konosuba. Agent Six is a combat operative for the Kisaragi Corporation, an evil secret organization bent on world domination. He and an android partner are sent to another planet to prepare it for invasion, but he'd rather goof off. It's an over-the-top, irreverent comedy for fans of Akatsuki's humor.
392: Cromartie High School by Eiji Nonaka (ADV) is an absurd comedy. Takashi Kamiyama is a nice, studious boy who enrolls at Cromartie High, a school full of tough delinquents. Among his new classmates are a robot that everyone treats as a normal student and a gorilla who never speaks. It's deadpan, surreal humor for readers who enjoy strange and silly jokes.
393: Kiss Me at the Stroke of Midnight by Rin Mikimoto (Kodansha) is a shojo romance with a Cinderella twist. Hinana Sakura is a hardworking high school girl with a part-time job and a quiet life. Then she meets Kaede Ayase, a famous young actor whose real personality is very different from his public image. It's a sweet, swoony love story for readers who enjoy fairy-tale romance.
394: Wave, Listen to Me! by Hiroaki Samura (Kodansha) is a seinen comedy. Minare Koda works at a curry restaurant in Sapporo. One night, after a bad breakup, she drunkenly rants to a stranger at a bar, who turns out to work in radio. The next day she hears her own rant broadcast on the air. It's a fast-talking, funny series for adult readers who enjoy sharp dialogue and messy, likable characters.
395: Saint Young Men by Hikaru Nakamura (Kodansha) is a gentle comedy. Jesus and Buddha decide to take a vacation on Earth, and they share a small apartment in a Tokyo suburb. They try to blend in while discovering everyday modern life, from shopping and blogging to visiting the bathhouse. It's a warm, good-natured series that pokes fun with affection, best for readers who enjoy quiet slice-of-life humor.
396: Lazy Dungeon Master by Nanaroku (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy. Keima wakes up in another world as a dungeon master, bound to a dungeon core that takes the form of a girl named Rokuko. His only real goal is to sleep as much as possible, so he builds a dungeon designed to run itself with as little work as possible. It's a laid-back, clever isekai for readers who like unusual heroes.
397: Wolf & Parchment by Isuna Hasekura (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure light novel and a follow-up to Spice and Wolf. Col, the boy who once traveled with Holo and Lawrence, is now a young man hoping to reform the Church. He sets out on a journey and is joined by Myuri, the spirited daughter of Holo and Lawrence. It's a thoughtful, warm adventure for Spice and Wolf fans.
399: Lizzie McGuire by Terri Minsky (Tokyopop) is a kids comedy cine-manga based on the Disney Channel TV show. Lizzie is a regular middle schooler dealing with friends, crushes, embarrassing moments, and her annoying little brother. Along with her best friends Miranda and Gordo, she gets through it all, while her animated inner self says what she's really thinking. It's light, funny fun for young fans of the show.
